method: GitHub issue search via `gh api search/issues?q=repo:holistics/dbml+<terms>`, direct issue retrieval via `gh api repos/holistics/dbml/issues/<n>`, and direct retrieval of the test fixture file via the GitHub Contents API
limitations: GitHub's code/issue search endpoints are keyword-based and can miss relevant issues that use different terminology (e.g. an issue about domain-scoped validation might not contain the literal words searched); the search was not exhaustive across all ~950 issues in the repository, only targeted keyword queries. Issue #142 and #222 concern the SQL-to-DBML import direction (sql2dbml / db2dbml, reverse-engineering from an existing database), not the DBML-authoring direction this survey cares about (hand-writing DBML text) — they are recorded as contrary evidence about tooling robustness generally, but do not by themselves show that composite or self-referencing FKs are unauthorable in DBML text (the language-level support is independently confirmed in source-dbml-grammar.json and by this fixture). The Oracle importer fixture demonstrates one self-referencing Ref per table (two different tables, each with exactly one self-ref), not three simultaneous self-referencing Refs on a single table, so it corroborates the general mechanism but not the specific 'three at once' cardinality needed for TASK_INSTANCE.

value_constraint_beyond_type_contrary_ch.citation: Issue #484, closed 2025-11-04, superseded by the now-documented checks{} block (source-dbml-grammar.json 'Check Definition' section)
value_constraint_beyond_type_contrary_ch.rationale: This issue is contrary evidence of a PAST gap, not a current one: a user in 2023 asked for exactly the CHECK-constraint capability that docs.md's 'Check Definition' section (source-dbml-grammar.json) now documents as shipped. The issue's closed state with a 2025-11-04 timestamp is consistent with — though does not by itself prove — the checks{} feature having been added to resolve it; this inference is flagged rather than stated as certain, since the issue's closing comment/linked PR was not separately read.

self_referencing_fk_import_direction.citation: Issue #222 '[Postgres] Import fails on self referencing composite key' (open/state not confirmed in this pass)
self_referencing_fk_import_direction.rationale: This is a bug in the reverse direction (sql2dbml/db2dbml importing FROM an existing database INTO DBML), not in hand-authoring DBML text. Recorded because it is exactly the kind of contrary evidence the brief's mandatory search requires, and because it is relevant if the eventual Gigacron workflow ever needs db2dbml to reverse-engineer DBML from a live database — a path this survey did not otherwise evaluate, since DBML is being assessed as an authoring format, not a reverse-engineering target.

cross_cutting_domain_id_convention.citation: No built-in lint/convention-assertion mechanism was found anywhere in dbml.dbdiagram.io/docs/, dbml.dbdiagram.io/syntax/enrichment-visualization/, or the @dbml/cli source read in source-dbml-tooling.json
cross_cutting_domain_id_convention.rationale: DBML's own validator (the Compiler used by @dbml/cli, see source-dbml-tooling.json) checks syntax and referential well-formedness only — nothing in the documented column/table/index/check settings expresses a cross-table, cross-cutting rule such as 'every table tagged as Domain-owned must carry a domain_id column'. This would require a workaround: a custom script consuming @dbml/core's parsed JSON model (via `dbml2sql`'s underlying Parser, or a hand-written script using the `@dbml/core` npm package's parser API) to walk every table definition and assert the convention itself, entirely outside DBML's own tooling — directly analogous to a 'workaround such as a custom lint script layered on top', per the research question's own framing.

contrary_evidence_search.result: Found four relevant limitation-adjacent issues (#142, #222, #249, #545), all concerning the SQL-import direction or SQL-export edge cases (capitalized enum type names, enum values containing spaces) rather than the DBML-authoring direction this survey evaluates. Found one issue (#484) requesting exactly the value-constraint capability that now appears to be shipped as checks{} (closed 2025-11-04). Found no issue, docs page, or 'known limitations' statement addressing the cross-cutting-convention validator question directly — its not-expressible classification rests on the absence of any such documented mechanism across the docs and CLI source examined, not on an explicit maintainer statement that it is unsupported; this absence-of-evidence is recorded as the search result itself, per the evidence policy's requirement to record a search even when it finds nothing on point.
